links.comparator_used: Manual review of 896 reports (manual chart review labeling)
links.outcome: Accuracy of automated NLP classification of final reports as the examination-level reference, versus manual review
links.effect: Sensitivity 99.5%, specificity 99.6%, κ 0.99 against manual review of 896 reports
links.tradeoff: Because radiologists viewed AI output before reporting, report-referenced results are presented as agreement rather than accuracy; discordant examinations still needed image review.
links.quote: Final reports, classified by natural language processing (NLP; validated against manual review of 896 reports: sensitivity 99.5%, specificity 99.6%, κ 0.99), served as the examination-level comparator; randomly selected discordant examinations were reviewed on images.

links.comparator_used: Aggregate examination-level performance across all examinations
links.outcome: Examination-level AI-report agreement by clinical indication, which exposed heterogeneity hidden by the overall figure
links.effect: Agreement was 98.6% for screening, 38.3% for oncologic and 32.6% for inpatient/emergency examinations; inpatient/emergency examinations contributed 76.1% of discordance. Overall positive percent agreement was 80.6%, negative percent agreement 37.8%, and κ 0.13.
links.quote: Agreement was 98.6% for screening, 38.3% for oncologic, and 32.6% for inpatient/emergency examinations, which contributed 76.1% of discordance.

design_hint: local postdeployment performance monitoring by indication with image review
